text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Yugoslavia and Croatia conclude several bilateral agreements and abolish visas for diplomatic and official passports during Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic's visit to Zagreb.
- Zastava cars has produced 3,621 cars in the July-September period falling short of its 6,000 car target, says deputy director Miljko Eric.
- Work has begun on digging of a new 600 to 1,000 metre deep shaft in the Bor copper mine which has 600 millon tonnes of copper ore. Mining work will be carried out by Polish firm FRG.
- Montgenegro airlines gets its first plane, plans to start operating by end of year.
- Yugoslavia's Aviogenex 707-200 Boeing plane is still blocked at Zurich airport since October 19 because of its debt of $700,000 to the Credit Lyonnais bank.
- Insolvency of the economy still poses a big problem, says institute for market research.

- The left coalition SPS-JUL-ND is in the lead in a poll conducted by the institute for social sciences with 45 percent of those polled, while 30 percent are for the the opposition coalition Zajedno. Serbian president Slobodan Milosevic is the most trustworthy politician, according to the poll.
- Election campaign blackout in Yugoslavia starts at midnight Thursday.
- Strikers of Belgrade city transport get beating instead of dialogue. Belgrade police unblocks the city transport garages, the interior ministry said in a statement.
- Military and prisoners will vote by mail, says federal election commission.

- Yugoslavia can expect to regulate its status in the IMF by end of year, and its cooperation with the Paris and London Club of creditors in the first quarter of 1997, says central bank Vice-governor Zarko Trbojevic.
- Conditions exist for explosion of the dinar exchange rate, and can be expected around the end of year, says economist Mladjan Dinkic.

- Montenegro's output has grown by 51.7 percent in the first nine months of this year over the same period in 1995 but there are enormous stocks of unsold finished products, the Montenegrin chamber of economy warned.
- Stability of the domestic currency has been maintained and there is no reason for it not to continue this way, says Yugoslav central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic.
